chunks: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi from Abdullah ibn Hammam al-Ansari from Muhammad ibn Ja'far from his father (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come over the people in which the pilgrimage of kings will be a leisure trip, and the pilgrimage of the wealthy will be trade, and the pilgrimage of the poor will be a request (for sustenance).'
ai.seo_question: What are the different motives for performing Hajj according to social status in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual decay of the Hajj ritual, where the sacred act is reduced to worldly pursuits: leisure for kings, commerce for the wealthy, and mere survival for the poor. It serves as a critique of the loss of *ikhlas* (sincerity) in religious practice, emphasizing that the true essence of Hajj is often overshadowed by social stratification and materialism.
